newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen mixed at open before NAPM, FOMC.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen mixed at open before NAPM, FOMC.

text.p: U.S. stocks were expected to open mixed on Tuesday ahead of the start of a two-day Federal Reserve policy maker meeting and the release of the National Association of Purchasing Managers report for June.
"The stock market will likely be mixed at the open, with some caution ahead of the FOMC meeting," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co.

The Federal Open Market Committee was widely expected to leave interest rates alone, but that would not necessarily prevent stocks and bonds from getting jitters, especially in a week full of economic data, analysts said.
In early trade, the Standard & Poor's 500 futures index was up 1.75 points at 892.00 but the long bond was down 5/32 at a 6.80 percent yield.
Both stocks and bonds were expected to watch the National Association of Purchasing Managers report for June, due at 1400 GMT, for signs of strength in the manufacturing sector.

"The market could sit around waiting for information," said Edgar Peters, chief investment strategist & director, asset allocation at PanAgora Asset Management Inc. "There will be volatility with all the economic news due out."
